item.title: Lady Bullpups take down circle, Augusta
item.description: The McPherson High girls’ basketball team may finally be finding its stride at the perfect moment. After navigating several early-season bumps under new head coach, Clint Kinnamon, the Lady Bullpups put together maybe their strongest week of the season while earning back-to-back road victories over Circle and Augusta, extending a win streak to three heading into the final stretch of the regular season.

item.title: McPherson wrestlers advance to state tournament
item.description: Eight McPherson Bullpups are headed to the state wrestling tournament in Salina. The two-day event begins Friday.

item.title: Bullpup swimmers finish 28th as Bohme delivers on Saturday
item.description: The McPherson High boys’ swim team battle through razor-thin margins at the Class 5-1A State Meet in Lenexa with sophomore Cooper Bohme powering the Bullpups to their only points of the weekend.. At the state meet, the top 16 teams/individuals from the preliminary swims on Friday move through to the finals on Saturday with the top-eight being the ‘A’ final to decide medalist order and the ‘B’ final to determine places ninth to sixteenth.

item.title: Hot Start, Tough Finish: Bullpup splits the week
item.description: With the regular season entering its final stretch, the McPherson Bullpups were ranked seventh in Class 4A last week before wrapping it up with a dominant win at Circle followed by a narrow, hard-fought loss at Augusta. Opening the week with a statement performance on Tuesday, McPherson rolled to a 59-28 victory over Circle as they controlled the game on both ends.

item.title: Lindsborg Museum to Release Pancake, Waffle Flour Based on Historical 80-Year-Old Smoky Valley Recipe
item.description: Vintage and “throwback” foods are a popular trend, but the story behind a new product coming from the Lindsborg Old Mill & Swedish Heritage Museum is like no other.

item.title: 3 steps to simplify tax prep so you can file on time
item.description: Spring is noted for the sense of rejuvenation it inspires when temperatures warm up and flowers begin to bloom. But in the United States, the onset of spring is followed shortly thereafter by tax season, which typically generates entirely different feelings than the first sight of spring blooms.

item.title: Kansas House passes election bills targeting noncitizens, advanced voting
item.description: TOPEKA — Kansas lawmakers could transform elections with a series of bills that squeeze advanced voting timelines, stamp out rare instances of noncitizen voting and tinker with some candidate filing and advocacy rules.

item.title: How a handful of states and districts could decide who runs Congress
item.description: WASHINGTON — Republicans and Democrats will spend billions of dollars and countless hours campaigning throughout the country ahead of November’s midterm elections, even though control of Congress likely will be decided by a relatively small number of toss-up races and the voters who actually turn out to cast a ballot for their preferred candidate. item.title: Kansas disaster declaration prepares state for World Cup visitor boom
item.description: TOPEKA — The 2026 North American FIFA World Cup prompted Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly to declare a state of disaster emergency in three counties, anticipating effects from four base camps in the Kansas City-area.

item.title: Wildfires scorch more than 300,000 acres in Kansas and northwest Oklahoma
item.description: Oklahoma fire crews are battling several wildfires that have consumed more than 300,000 acres in Oklahoma and Kansas. According to NASA’s fire information system there are a handful of small wildfires in eastern Oklahoma, with four massive blazes in western Oklahoma.
